commitResults.messageTitle: Level 4: Add Todo, Deadline, and Event types
commitResults.messageBody:
All tasks are a single Task with only a description and a done flag.

Users need three kinds of work: todos with no date, deadlines due by a
date/time, and events with a start and an end. Dates can stay as
strings at this increment.

Let's,
* add Todo, Deadline, and Event as subclasses of Task
* add tasks with todo, deadline /by, and event /from /to
* show [T], [D], and [E] (and by/from/to text) in list, mark, and unmark

Keeping dates as strings matches Level 4. Real date parsing can wait
until a later increment.

Bad input such as an empty todo or an unknown word either crashes the
chatbot or is treated as a new task.
Users need a clear error and a chance to try again, without the list
changing.
Handle invalid chatbot commands for the following cases:
* empty todo description
* unknown commands
* blank input
* deadline missing a name or /by
* event missing a name, /from, or /to
* mark/unmark with a missing, non-numeric, or out-of-range number
Catch WodanException in the main loop, print the message, and keep
listening. A chatbot-specific exception keeps these errors separate
from Java's built-in ones, and the messages say how to correct the
command.

Tasks can be added, listed, and marked, but there is no way to remove one.
Users need to delete a quest by its list number and see what was removed.
Add the following:
* a delete N command that removes that task from the list
* a confirmation that prints the removed task and the new list size
* toString() on Todo, Deadline, and Event so add, list, mark, unmark, and
  delete share one print format
* the same missing/invalid number checks used by mark and unmark
Each subclass owns its [T]/[D]/[E] line, so Wodan does not switch on type
when printing.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Enums: Represent commands with Command enum
commitResults.messageBody:
The main loop switches on raw strings such as todo and delete.
A mistyped word is easy to miss, and every new command has to be added
as another quoted case.
Add the following:
* a Command enum for todo, deadline, event, list, mark, unmark, delete,
  and bye
* Command.parse to turn the first word into that enum
* a switch on Command instead of on String
An enum lists the legal commands in one place. Unknown words fail in
parse, and the compiler can catch a missing case.

commitResults.messageTitle: implement storage of deadline as LocalDateTime object.
Extract Ui to isolate console input and output from Wodan.
commitResults.messageBody:
Wodan still decides which replies to show, but all Scanner and System.out use now go through Ui. This is the first step of the Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList split and keeps chatbot wording unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList to encapsulate in-memory task operations.
commitResults.messageBody:
Wodan now adds, deletes, and queries tasks through TaskList instead of
mutating an ArrayList directly. Storage still reads and writes ArrayList
so file I/O stays separate from list operations.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser to interpret user command lines.
commitResults.messageBody:
Wodan now asks Parser for the command word, arguments, task objects, and
list numbers, so command-string rules live in one place instead of the
main loop. Reply text and list/storage updates stay in Wodan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Turn Wodan into a coordinator with constructor and run.
commitResults.messageBody:
Wodan now holds Ui, Storage, and TaskList, loads the save file in the
constructor, and runs the command loop from run(). Storage takes the
file path from Wodan so the save location is no longer hardcoded there.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace the command switch with Command objects.
commitResults.messageBody:
Wodan now parses a line into a Command and calls execute/isExit, so each
user action lives in its own class. The old Command enum is renamed to
CommandWord so Parser can still map the first token. Printed output is
unchanged; run() does not wrap every reply in extra divider lines.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
